summary: Verified the requested paper-level target c098, covering all four supplement_changes entries; supplement_added is empty. Read the complete main-paper and supplement markdown conversions, including references and all appendices. Extracted all eight supplement PDF pages with PyMuPDF, recovered Table D.1 with find_tables(), and inspected the information-flow and prompt-template figures in memory. Checked the retained main-paper results against their cited PDF pages 10 and 12-14, and the design and measurement definitions against PDF pages 8-11. The supplement title page supports source.supplement_used. Appendix D, Table D.1 (supplement PDF p. 6, printed p. 4), confirms that outcomes are calculated per brainstorming session, separately for human-origin ideas and combined human/GLM ideas. It defines Good-Idea-Count as the number of long-list ideas exceeding the average GPT-4 rating across long lists from all sessions, without printing a numerical cutoff. Main PDF p. 13 (printed p. 1035) does print 3.396 both as the novelty cutoff in Sect. 4.1 and as the treatment mean for judge-rated dyad novelty in Sect. 4.2; the supplement does not resolve this duplication, so retaining the open item and the printed values is correct. The supplement adds no eligible contrast, outcome result, participant count, or preregistered primary designation. Appendix C contains survey instruments, and Appendix E contains qualitative response codes; these do not supply eligible output-based estimates. All four logged changes agree with the current extraction fields and concern supplement availability or explanatory text. No estimate, study, statistic, or count field is changed in the log, and the retained numerical results for all 16 estimates agree with the main PDF and the correct outcome and arm contrast. The printed common analytic sample is 75. The four human-level shortlist-rating records correctly leave counts null because final analysis counts are not printed; group sizes 38 and 37 are not labeled by arm. The requested question, construct, measure, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, outcome_timing, within_person, comparison_type, se_basis, and preregistered_primary codes are consistent with the methods and Appendix D. Each session contains one human, so participant-level coding is appropriate for both human and dyad outcomes. The supplement-availability limitation can be closed; the remaining disclosed limitations are not resolved by the supplement. No supplement-pass error was found.
